html:
Champagne and Aishihik is the homeland of the Champagne and Aishihik First Nations in the southwest Yukon, around Haines Junction and the Aishihik Lake country. Its people are mostly Southern Tutchone, an Athabaskan people, with Tlingit ties.

They hunted caribou, moose and sheep, fished for salmon in the Alsek basin and traded with the coastal Tlingit along trails over the mountains. Their land borders the great icefields of Kluane.

Gold seekers came through during the Klondike Gold Rush of the 1890s, and in 1942 the Alaska Highway cut across their land. In 1993 they were among the first four Yukon First Nations to sign final land claim and self-government agreements.
